title: Forecasting Associations, Not Interventions: A Preregistered Causal Audit of Covariate-Aware Time Series Foundation Models

primary_sources.paraphrase: Single-author arXiv v1, 22 Oct 2026. Abstract reports that four covariate-aware TSFMs answer what-if queries like observational regression, on synthetic structural models and two physical systems.

Full text: slope table per model with bootstrap intervals, preregistration described (preregister.yaml, tag prereg-freeze, three amendments), and Appendix C saying code and prereg file come with the final version.

claims.text: Chronos-2, TiRex-2 and TimesFM-2.5 (with XReg) respond more confounded than regression; impact-coefficient slopes 1.3-1.8 on synthetic structural models.
TabPFN-TS tracks the reference line with slope about 1.00 (95% CI 0.85-1.13), so it is associational but not more confounded than regression.
When the effect is identifiable, least squares recovers 100% of the true effect difference, Chronos-2 75%, TiRex-2 34%.
A short interventional post-training with pretraining-prior replay cuts the gap by 52-61% at +1-3% MASE.

relevance.rationale: Targets are synthetic series and two physical rigs, not electric load; the readout is the response at the first intervened step, not a 168 h forecast. Covariates are control variables in what-if queries, not known-future weather used to improve accuracy. It bears on how to read the covariate response of Chronos-2, which we run, but does not test forecast accuracy.

checks.notes: Pre-registration is described in the paper (preregister.yaml, tag prereg-freeze, three amendments), but Appendix C says the file, amendment log and code will be released with the final version; no public record was found, so I did not mark it yes. Independent replication: none found. Won (arXiv:2610.08118, forced engineering systems, H=128) and a Zenodo record on synthetic generators are related but test different questions; they are in the ledger but not cited as replication. 'no' rests on one You.com research call plus those two sources, not an exhaustive search. Central model: Chronos-2 (first in the headline list); its weights commit date was not fetched, so training_overlap_risk is unknown, and its licence was not verified from the model card. The headline comparison (confounding gap on synthetic what-if queries) is not what our benchmark measures, so ACCEPT_RUN does not apply. Evidence strength weak: numbers with intervals but no released code or data at this version, and the test unit is synthetic cells, not a test window of at least 90 days.

label: PARTIAL
label_reason: Sourced and about the covariate behaviour of a model we run (Chronos-2), but evidence is weak (no released code or preregistration record yet, one author, synthetic data) and its headline measure is a confounding gap, not week-ahead load error. It cannot be re-measured on our benchmark as a transfer test; use it as context for reading the Chronos-2 temperature result.
implementation_hint: Chronos-2 runs via models/chronos2.py (amazon/chronos-2). The paper's TiRex-2, TabPFN-TS and TimesFM-2.5 XReg setups are not needed for our primary comparison. Reproducing the confounding gap would need the authors' unreleased code.
